subject: Renewal discussion: upgrade path for reserved GPUs and overflow handling
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.m@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@acmehealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 03 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion: upgrade path for reserved GPUs and overflow handling

Samira / Acme procurement team —

Thanks again for the productive renewal planning call last week. Per our conversation I wanted to lay out two pragmatic upgrade paths for your Dedicated pool and how we can handle burst / overflow during the new term. We framed this to match the Acme latency-sensitive inference workloads you described.

Quick summary of the ask: Acme wants to increase reserved capacity for the Q4 year-over-year rollout (targeting a 2x throughput increase), maintain predictable baseline throughput for SLAs, and agree on an overflow plan for traffic spikes.

Option A — Reserved-first + pay-as-you-go overflow
- Reserved: add 16 x A100 equivalent GPUs into your dedicated pool (exclusive). Baseline throughput guarantee: 1.5M tokens/min with 99.5% availability SLA (route-level).
- Overflow: when reserved pool is saturated, requests spill to Redwood hosted on-demand capacity at a pre-negotiated burst rate (discounted multiplier on list). Pay only for overflow token usage. No changes to request routing on your side.

Option B — Hard cap + graceful degradation
- Reserved: add 16 x A100 equivalent GPUs, baseline throughput guarantee: same as above.
- Hard cap: once reserved pool reaches capacity, additional requests are queued or served by an agreed degraded path (quantized model variant, lower concurrency) to keep cost predictable. No on-demand billing beyond reserved commitment.

Operational tradeoffs we highlighted:
- Option A maximizes availability during spikes but introduces variable spend; ideal if Acme prefers performance-first.
- Option B keeps spend fixed but may increase tail latency or slightly degrade quality under peak.

Questions for you:
1) Do you prefer the flexibility of overflow billing (Option A) or the cost certainty of a hard cap (Option B)?
2) If you prefer overflow, would a capped monthly overspend commitment (e.g., up to 30% of reserved spend at discounted rates) be acceptable?
3) Timeline — what sign date do you need to hit to secure the A100 pool by Nov 15?

Attached: procurement_requirements.pdf (from your team) — I pulled the checklist and flagged items we'll need for the amendment.

If helpful, Vanessa and Karthik are copied to propose a concrete pricing matrix and the technical rollout plan. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call to close this next week.

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael.m@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Samira Khan <samira.k@acmehealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.m@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: upgrade path for reserved GPUs and overflow handling

Rafael —

Thanks for the clear options. A couple of clarifying questions from my side before I loop procurement formally: 

- Can you break down the expected monthly cost delta between Option A and Option B assuming our historical peak patterns (I can share a 6-month token histogram if helpful).
- For Option A, what would the overflow discount tiers look like (e.g., up to 20% spill, 20–50%, >50%)? We need predictable bands to present to finance.
- For Option B, what are the exact SLAs and how will Redwood signal queued vs degraded responses? We need clear behavior for our downstream systems.

Procurement also asked for SOC2 evidence and the standard MSA amendment language that covers committed GPU counts and billing treatment for overflow. I attached the procurement checklist you referenced earlier — filing that under procurement_requirements.pdf.

From a product preference, I lean toward a hybrid approach: baseline reserved for predictable traffic but with a limited overflow allowance so customer-facing endpoints stay responsive during marketing-driven spikes. My ask: can Redwood propose a hybrid pricing model and a one-quarter trial or ramp period?

If you can send a short write-up and indicative numbers by EOD Wednesday I will get procurement engaged and provide the token histogram.

Best,
Samira Khan
Director, ML Platforms — Acme Health
samira.k@acmehealth.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@acmehealth.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.m@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 05 Oct 2027 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: upgrade path for reserved GPUs and overflow handling

Samira / team —

Thanks for the prompt feedback. Rafael asked me to draft a practical hybrid we can quote quickly. High-level proposal below — I will attach a matrix (hybrid_pricing_matrix.xlsx) with values and examples tied to your historical token distribution.

Hybrid proposal (recommended):
- Reserved pool: +16 A100 equivalent GPUs, dedicated to Acme. Baseline SLA: 99.9% availability per route, latency SLOs defined per endpoint.
- Overflow allowance: up to 30% of reserved token consumption per month at a fixed discounted overflow rate (X% off list). Overflow beyond 30% will follow Option A-style pay-as-you-go at a higher discounted rate, or automatically trigger model swap to a pre-approved quantized variant to reduce CPU/GPU cost.
- Fail-safe: If both reserved and overflow tiers are saturated, Redwood will fallback to a "degraded path" (lower-quality, lower-latency model) for non-critical inference routes; critical routes preserve baseline at the expense of latency for non-critical routes.
- Ramp period: 90-day ramp (month 1: 50% reserved activation, month 2: 75%, month 3: 100%) to allow warm-pool tuning and KV cache warmup. During ramp, overflow is billed at the same discounted overflow rate but with a pro-rated cap.

Operational notes:
- We'll implement route-level policies so you can choose which endpoints get overflow priority.
- We'll include an automated alerting policy and daily token spend cap guard that notifies both teams and blocks overflow if a manual stop is requested.
- We can commit to an SLA addendum for baseline throughput; overflow usage has a best-effort latency target and the discounted billing tiers reflect that.

I'll send a pricing matrix and draft amendment for review by Wednesday EOD. Rafael — can you confirm the exact A100 SKU equivalence Acme prefers and whether they need HBM sizing called out?

— Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Enterprise Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.m@redwood.ai>, Samira Khan <samira.k@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Oct 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: upgrade path for reserved GPUs and overflow handling

Quick technical confirmation from infra side —

We can support the hybrid approach Vanessa outlined. A few implementation bullets: 
- Routing: implement priority-based routing with a short-tail circuit breaker for overflow events. Requests assigned overflow priority will automatically be routed to the on-demand pool unless they hit the monthly overflow cap.
- Model swap: pre-staged quantized variants can be used as the degraded path; KV cache migration will be handled by parallel warm copies to avoid cold-start tail latency. Expect some transient token-rate degradation during the first 24 hours of ramp if cache is cold.
- SLA / telemetry: we'll publish route-level latency percentiles and a daily token consumption dashboard to Acme's console. We can instrument a 2-hour rolling window metric for spill rate and set automated notifications at 60%, 80%, and 100% of overflow allowance.

I'll add the technical appendix to the draft amendment. Also linking our internal playbook for routing and warm-pools: https://redwood.internal/notes/route-burst-playbook

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Product Manager, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

From: Samira Khan <samira.k@acmehealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.m@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 06 Oct 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: upgrade path for reserved GPUs and overflow handling

Team —

This looks like exactly the pragmatic approach we were hoping for. Acme is comfortable with the hybrid plan: reserved + 30% overflow band + model-swap fail-safe. Procurement will expect a written amendment and an illustrative 12-month quote (line items: reserved GPUs, overflow allowance, overflow rate tiers, ramp credits, and SLA addendum). Net-30 invoicing is preferred.

Next steps from Acme: I'll share the token histogram by EOD Thursday and copy Procurement to get the formal PO ready. Please include SOC2 evidence and the MSA amendment language in the packet.

Thanks all — Samira
Procurement contact: Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>
